newsitem.title: USA: First Team Sports hurt by weaker outlook.
newsitem.headline: First Team Sports hurt by weaker outlook.

text.p: First Team Sports Inc's forecast of a second-quarter earnings shortfall hurt the stock Wednesday, said analysts were revising their projections for the Minneapolis-based maker of in-line roller skates.
Hambrecht & Quist analyst Sally Hale Young said her $1.32 per share estimate for the fiscal year will come down dramatically.
First Team said sales for the second quarter, ending August 31, are seen in a range of $15 to $16 million, and earnings at $0.03 to $0.07 a share, below Wall Street expectations.
First Team was trading at 8-1/2, off 1-1/4.
"First Team will continue to be a player in the (in-line skates) industry," Young said.
She added that the expected shortfall in sales and earnings reflects continuing weakness at the retail level but not the vitality of the sport or the potential for First Team.
Analyst Robert Marvin of Seidler Cos also said he was reviewing his estimates on First Team.
"We had lowered our rating on the company to neutral earlier and brought the quarter's estimate down to $0.20 per share," he said. "Obviously, that's not low enough."
